newsitem.title: UK: London stocks outlook -- focus on UK economy.
newsitem.headline: London stocks outlook -- focus on UK economy.

text.p: A hefty batch of British economic indicators is likely to preoccupy the stock market next week, amid heightened worries over the pace of growth, analysts and traders said on Friday.

After the Bank of England on Thursday hiked its base lending rate by a quarter point to 6.75 percent, markets were seen on alert for any indicators of continuing economic strength likely to increase the risk of further increases.
Wednesday's jobs report for June, along with Monday's producer price figures, will come under close scrutiny for any fresh signs that the pace of growth is stoking inflationary pressures.

"I suspect there are hazards ahead and the market will be sensitive to any disappointments in these figures," said Richard Jeffrey, chief economist at brokerage Charterhouse Tilney. "The market may be more vulnerable to bad news than it had been."
Fresh signs of economic strength were also likely to add further impetus to the soaring pound, which stood poised to rise above three marks for the first time in more than six years.

The strength of sterling was seen keeping up the pressure on the earnings of exporters and international stocks, with the likes of Imperial Chemical Industries Plc (ICI) and British Steel Plc already subject to a succession of downgrades.

A string of economic reports in the U.S. next week, including Tuesday's retail sales report for June and Wednesday's consumer price report, could also give markets pause for thought on both sides of the Atlantic.

Yet participants also saw little reason to be particularly negative on the British stock market, which has shimmied past a series of negative developments in recent days including a budget which removed tax perks on shares for pension funds.

Domestic investment institutions remain cash rich and seem prepared to inject funds into selected sectors where domestic growth is welcome news -- such as food retailers and brewers, both up strongly in the past week.
Equally some overseas investors view blue chip British equities as relatively good value, having underperformed leading continual bourses this year.
It is this flow of funds into the market which provides the most potent bullish signal, analysts said.

"Liquidity is being funnelled in from overseas and we have seen some big moves in some very focused areas," said Steve Wright, investment strategist at BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays Bank.
Nick Glydon, analyst at investment bank Robert Fleming, said recent gains in consumer-oriented stocks were a positive signal for the market overall.
"With sterling still going up a lot of stocks are being badly affected," Glydon said, "but all of a sudden some other interesting things are going on and that gives some confidence in the market."
Glydon noted that a rise in Britain's FTSE 100 index so far this year had been driven largely by bank and drug stocks, adding that a rise in other sectors was a welcome signal.
"The market is looking more healthy now than it has for some time," Glydon said, adding that a break upwards through 4,800 by the FTSE 100 could be a further positive sign.
The index was up 25.0 points at 4,792.8 by 1219 GMT on Friday, not far from its record 4,879.0 set on July 4.
"4,800 doesn't mean a lot but it is a nice round number," Glydon said. "A move above that level would probably be seen as a bullish signal."
